column1: # Kazakhstan, kz.qmdb: QMDB (muftyat.kz), documented in the site's own code as praytimes.js ISNA
# 15/15, Hanafi, AngleBased high-latitude rule, sunrise -3/Dhuhr,Asr,Maghrib +3 below 48N and -5/+5
# at or above it (terms not found; used only to fit and prove). First fit on Almaty (43.24N, below
# 48) and Astana (51.13N, at or above 48, the ≥48N variant) over Jan-Jun 2026 alone, held out on
# the same two cities' Jul-Dec 2026: high summer (Jul-Sep) showed a few 1-minute-early Fajr/Asr/
# Isha days at both cities (proof.md), so Jul-Dec is folded into the fit set too (a season the
# solstice-adjacent half did not cover); nothing is held out. The API's own "imsak" field (= Fajr +
# End of eating (audit of 3 Oct 2026, before Ramadan 1448): the fast begins at QMDB's printed Fajr (the API's later "imsak" is
# not used), so the Fajr column is also checked as the end of eating (F+E). At and above 48N the end
# of eating carries its own margin and a recorded limit (CentralAsia.kt). Fix round (3 Oct 2026): QMDB's
# 2026 and 2027 tables for Astana, Kokshetau, Kostanay, Pavlodar and Petropavl (54.9N), fetched from the
# same API, broke Astana's -221 s (123 late ends, up to 2 min, Apr-Jun, mostly at Petropavl); the margin is
# refitted on all of them (-374 s).
# Northern round (3 Oct 2026): those tables, with Almaty's 2027, are pinned as the kz-qmdb monitor fetched
# The Almaty and Astana 2026 captures equal the off_ala/off_ast tables above, so they get no second row.
# At the 2026-only margins Astana's 2027 Fajr was 1 min early on 7 July days and the northern cities' Isha on
# 4 August days, so the starts are refitted: Astana 2027, Kokshetau, Pavlodar and Petropavl are fit rows
# (they decide Fajr, Isha, Asr and Maghrib, as they decided the end of eating); Almaty 2027 and Kostanay
# (its own zone, the farthest west) are held out. Northern lateness grows to Petropavl and is recorded as
# kz.qmdb's Fajr (8 min) and Isha (5 min) limits (CentralAsia.kt, proof 7f).
# North-west round (6 Oct 2026): 23 more of QMDB's own places from its city list (api.muftyat.kz/cities/), pinned as the
# kz-qmdb fetcher read them on 6 Oct 2026 (archive/tables/pinned/kz-qmdb/2026-10-06/; raw JSON in
# archive/raw/monitor/kz-qmdb/2026-10-06/, the city list in archive/raw/manual/kz-qmdb/2026-10-06/): north of Petropavl
# to its northernmost (Isakovka 55.4N, Krasny Yar, Kulomzino); the west and every zone of the app's Kazakh cities (Oral
# and Aksay, Asia/Oral; Aktobe, Khromtau and Shalqar, Asia/Aqtobe; Atyrau, Makat and Oteshqali Atambayev, Asia/Atyrau;
# Aktau, Asia/Aqtau; Kyzylorda, Asia/Qyzylorda); the south to QMDB's southernmost (Shymkent; Zhenis, 40.6N); 46-48N,
# where QMDB's offsets stay +-3 but its AngleBased rule binds around the solstice (Oteshqali Atambayev, QMDB's place
# nearest 48N, and Ayagoz, with Shalqar, Atyrau, Mamyrsu and Makat); and places just either side of the engine's 0.1 deg
# curve steps (Vagulino, Bugrovoe, Pulemetovka, Spasovka, Khromtau, Arkalyk, Oskemen, Mamyrsu, Makat, Kulomzino). All
# went in first as test rows at the margins of 3 Oct: no start was early at the fourteen places north, west, south and
# from 46 to 48N, but the end of eating came after QMDB's printed Fajr at Kulomzino (2 days, 1 min) and from 46 to 48N
# (up to 3 min, late May to mid-June), and Isha went 1 min over its 5-min limit north of Petropavl; at the curve-step
# places Fajr was 1 min early at QMDB's own Bugrovoe, Spasovka and Oskemen (27 days, the solstice to mid-August), whose
# curve the 0.1 deg grid read about 0.05 deg south of them, and the end of eating 1 min late at Vagulino (2 days). Fixed
# in the registry (CentralAsia.kt, TwilightCurves.kt, proof 7f): the curves are also read at each place's own latitude
# (each slot the later start, the earlier end), a 46-48N end-of-eating margin (-150 s), Asr and Maghrib refitted later
# (-6, -14), and Isha's limit 6 min. Fit rows: Isakovka and Krasny Yar (the edge) and Oteshqali Atambayev and Ayagoz
# (the band's top); the other 19 are held out.
